raw_response:
My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I have about 8 mu. There is no question what I grow — wheat in winter, corn in summer. That is what this land is for. That is what my neighbors grow. That is what the buyers come for.

I will plant winter wheat in October after the summer corn is off. I get my seed from the county seed station — the Jimai variety they've been selling around here for years. It does well on my soil. I put down compound fertilizer when I sow, then come back with urea in March when the plants start jointing. I water three times: once before the ground freezes in November to help the roots settle, once at jointing in April, and once when the grain is filling in May. I spray twice — once in spring when the aphids come, once if I see powdery mildew. I use the rotary tiller. My son helped me get a small tractor. No ploughing deep anymore, my back won't allow it and the machine is easier.

After wheat harvest in June I plant corn the same day or next day. Xianyu 335 hybrid seed — everyone here uses it, the yield is reliable. I put down urea once at the big flare stage in July. Usually corn catches the summer rains and I only irrigate once, maybe twice if August is dry. I spray once or twice for stem borers and army worm.

I do not try new crops. At 63, I know what works. My land is flat, the well is still working, and wheat-corn pays my costs.
